answer:
Official Product Roadmap (NL-014) places the Microsoft Teams integration in “Under Active Design and Planning” with a release target of Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November) and a restricted pilot starting October 2026; currently only the Slack connector is in limited pilot [NL-014#NL-014-S07]. NL-015 confirms the Teams integration stays in design phase for Q4, with development expected in early 2027, and that engineering resources are prioritized for the OCR Pipeline [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

Informal sales claims contradict this. In NL-023, Marcus Reed tells a prospect the Teams integration is “right around the corner,” “almost ready for general release,” and could be enabled for a July pilot [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. Internal Slack exchanges show Marcus asking for an insecure “alpha” or custom one-off build, but product, infrastructure, and engineering all reject it, noting the existing demo is a “toy” with zero tenant isolation, zero permission mapping, zero SSO, and no formatting or citation links [NL-027#NL-027-S03][NL-027#NL-027-S04]. The sales playbook (NL-009) itself instructs reps not to guarantee specific launch dates and to treat roadmap dates as targets, not contractual commitments [NL-009#NL-009-S08].

Thus, the official roadmap states the Teams integration is not available until Q4 2026 at earliest, while informal sales/Slack claims overstate readiness and propose deployments that would violate security and compliance requirements.
